requirements.requirement: Require new user passwords to be at least 12 characters long (minlen=12) on node1
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf was edited to add 'minlen = 12' via sudo (cmd-514e4170c0fb4b3e) and confirmed present both immediately after the edit and after a full node restart (cmd-db3257c36231425b), matching PAM wiring to pam_pwquality via requisite in system-auth/password-auth.

requirements.requirement: Require new user passwords to use at least three different character classes (minclass=3) on node1
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf was edited to add 'minclass = 3' in the same operation, confirmed present pre- and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Policy is actually enforced for new user password changes (not just configured)
requirements.summary: Live PAM password-change attempts as the non-root test user (su - pwtestuser -c passwd) show a short password rejected ('password is shorter than 11 characters'), a 12+ char password with only 2 classes rejected ('password contains less than 3 character classes'), and a 12+ char 3-class password accepted (exit 0). Note the earlier root-context 'sudo passwd pwtestuser' call (cmd-d225d74e79de4fbc) bypassed the check as expected for root and was correctly not relied on as the enforcement proof; the executor used the su-based non-root flow for the actual enforcement test, which is the correct method.

requirements.requirement: Configuration and enforcement survive a node restart (durability)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (d7a80301...) and healthy config were captured (cmd-5e3ffe3552764ede), a backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned an acknowledgement before disconnect (cmd-d7692a8384a943ca), a subsequent poll timed out confirming the node went down (cmd-027f55fa912046ab), a later poll succeeded with a new boot_id (6930b99c...) and fresh uptime (cmd-6a0877df9bc4464b), matching the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots exactly. Post-restart, pwquality.conf/PAM config were re-verified intact (cmd-db3257c36231425b) and a fresh live PAM enforcement test with a second user again rejected a non-compliant password and accepted a compliant one (cmd-92313573caa540a1), demonstrating the full pre-disruption/disruption/recovery cycle with functional verification at each stage.

overall_summary: The executor configured minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf on node1, verified via live PAM-driven passwd attempts (as the non-root target user) that short and low-diversity passwords are rejected and compliant passwords are accepted, and confirmed both the configuration and live enforcement persist correctly across a full, directly observed node restart (matching pre/post boot identities from the fixed lifecycle snapshots). Test users used for verification were removed. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, well-corroborated evidence.
limitations: No independent verification beyond the captured command transcripts was possible; correctness relies on the pwquality error strings and passwd exit codes as reported.
A minor leftover file (/tmp/reboot.log) from the restart command was not cleaned up, though it is low-risk and does not affect password-policy functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: Test users pwtestuser and pwtestuser2 were created to validate enforcement and both were deleted afterward, confirmed via failed 'id' lookups (cmd-5d784007d5f94e2f, cmd-e0ddf1015ef54eef) — a bounded, fully-reverted, necessary mutation for verification. One minor unreverted artifact: /tmp/reboot.log, created as the stdout/stderr redirection target for the backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' command (cmd-d7692a8384a943ca), remains present in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot and was not cleaned up. This is low-risk, non-sensitive residue incidental to a necessary restart-evidence step, not a broad or destructive change. No failed services, no problematic listening-socket changes beyond expected restart-induced PID/ephemeral differences, and no package-state damage were observed in the lifecycle comparison.
